notes: Seeded detection corpus for the database persona (2026-08-19 corpus-expansion). Same
self-contained-diff, AND-of-OR mustMatch grading evaluate-testing-charter.mjs already uses
for the testing, security, architecture and performance corpora -- no code changes needed,
One defect fixture per Flag rule in the database charter (destructive migration on a column
still referenced by deployed code, a locking NOT NULL DEFAULT migration on a large table, a
migration with no path backwards once partially applied, an unindexed filter on an unbounded
table, string-interpolated SQL), each paired with a near-miss clean control drawn from the
charter's own Do-not-flag list: the identical NOT NULL DEFAULT shape on a table the same
migration creates (no existing rows, no lock), an interpolated identifier that is allowlist-
validated rather than raw user text, and a missing index on a report query that is explicitly
Run candidate-only (no charter rewrite here to A/B against a baseline snapshot):

fixtures.title: Drop the legacy name columns now that display_name exists
fixtures.summary: Migration 0057 drops customers.first_name and customers.last_name, but getCustomerCard.js -- shown in the same diff with an unrelated added field -- still selects both columns, so the query will start failing (or the deploy must be perfectly sequenced) the moment this migration runs.

fixtures.title: Add preferred_locale to orders, defaulting to en-US
fixtures.summary: The new orders.preferred_locale column is changed from a plain nullable ADD COLUMN to NOT NULL DEFAULT 'en-US' -- on a table this write-heavy, that rewrites/locks every existing row instead of backfilling in a separate, non-blocking step.

fixtures.title: Rename orders.total to orders.total_cents
fixtures.summary: A single migration adds total_cents, backfills it, drops the original total column, then renames total_cents back to total -- all as one non-atomic sequence. If it fails after the DROP but before the RENAME, the orders table is left with no total column and no defined way back; the safe two-migration add-then-backfill-then-drop-later sequence this file replaced is gone.

fixtures.title: Filter customer orders by fulfillment status
fixtures.summary: The query gains a filter predicate on orders.fulfillment_status, but the migration in the same diff adds that column with no index -- on a table growing ~40k rows/day, this filter will do a full table scan that gets slower every day.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+-- Migration 0060: add fulfillment_status to orders for the new filter UI.
+-- orders grows by roughly 40k rows/day in production.
+ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN fulfillment_status TEXT;

fixtures.title: Let the admin orders table sort by a caller-chosen column
fixtures.summary: The query moves from a fully parameterised statement to a template literal that interpolates both the status value and the caller-supplied sortColumn directly into the SQL text, with no allowlist or validation on either -- a classic SQL-injection sink through the new sort parameter.

fixtures.title: Add a rollout_percent column while creating feature_flags
fixtures.summary: Control: NOT NULL DEFAULT is added to a column on a table this same migration is creating with CREATE TABLE -- the surface pattern from the locking-migration defect (NOT NULL DEFAULT) is present, but there are zero existing rows to rewrite and no lock risk, because the table does not exist yet.

files.patch:
@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@
--- Migration 0061: create the feature_flags table.
+-- Migration 0061: create feature_flags and seed the initial rollout gate.
 CREATE TABLE feature_flags (
   id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
   key TEXT NOT NULL,
-  enabled BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false
+  enabled BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
+  rollout_percent INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
 );

fixtures.title: Restrict the admin sort column to a fixed allowlist
fixtures.summary: Control: sortColumn is still spliced into a template literal for ORDER BY, but only after being checked against a fixed Set of known-safe column names -- an attacker cannot supply arbitrary SQL text through it, and the actual user-controlled value (status) stays fully parameterised via $1. Surface pattern matches the SQL-injection defect fixture; the rule (unvalidated untrusted input reaching SQL) does not.

fixtures.title: Narrow the quarterly compliance report to a date range
fixtures.summary: Control: this query filters orders with no supporting composite index, the same surface shape as the missing-index defect fixture, but the function is explicitly a manually-triggered admin cron job that runs once per quarter, never on a request path -- exactly the case the charter's own do-not-flag list carves out ('queries that run rarely or off the request path').
